source.version: Journal version of record: Research in Engineering Design (2026) 37:34, doi 10.1007/s00163-026-00497-x; received 3 April 2026, revised 30 June 2026, accepted 13 July 2026, published online 31 August 2026 (p. 1). The journal labels it 'REVIEW ARTICLE', but the content is an original experiment.
source.title_on_document: Human or model? A four-factor experimental study of design experience and image-generation alignment strategies in industrial product ideation

supplement.holds: The paper refers to no supplementary material or online appendix. All statistics are in Tables 3 to 7 (pp. 9, 11, 12, 14, 15).

paper_design_summary: Sixty lab participants, grouped by measured design experience (3 levels) and AIGC tool proficiency (2 levels), each generated motorcycle concept images in four 10-minute conditions: Midjourney V6 or ChatGPT-4o image generation, crossed with concrete or abstract prompts, with condition order set by a 4 x 4 balanced Latin square. Each participant submitted one representative image per condition; two senior product-design experts rated each image for quality and novelty and coded design attributes for an image-level attribute diversity score. There is no no-AI condition: every condition uses a generative image tool.

studies.label: Motorcycle concept ideation, 3 (EXP) x 2 (ATP) x 2 (IGAS: Midjourney V6 vs ChatGPT-4o) x 2 (prompt type) mixed design

assignment.what_was_assigned: Within person: every participant completed all four conditions (image tool Midjourney V6 vs ChatGPT-4o, crossed with concrete vs abstract prompts); the order of the four tasks was set by a 4 x 4 balanced Latin square. The paper does not say that participants were randomly allocated to Latin-square sequences. The between-subjects factors (design experience, AIGC tool proficiency) are measured traits from a pre-test questionnaire, not assigned.
assignment.quote: To control for order effects, task sequences were assigned using a 4 × 4 balanced Latin square design.
assignment.locator: p. 7, Sect. 3.3 (Procedure); design framework p. 6, Sect. 3.2.2; grouping by questionnaire p. 5, Sect. 3.1
assignment.prereg_locator: No preregistration mentioned; an a priori G*Power analysis is reported (p. 5, Sect. 3.1).

arms.name: Condition A: Midjourney V6 + concrete prompts (IGAS0, PT0)
arms.description: Midjourney V6 with default resolution, random seeds, style setting at middle (about 750); participants told to use terms for form, material, colour, structure, style.

arms.name: Condition B: Midjourney V6 + abstract prompts (IGAS0, PT1)
arms.description: Midjourney V6; participants told to use metaphorical, emotional, atmospheric, or cross-domain descriptors.

arms.name: Condition C: ChatGPT-4o + concrete prompts (IGAS1, PT0)
arms.description: ChatGPT-4o image generation, new chat window per task; concrete prompts.

arms.name: Condition D: ChatGPT-4o + abstract prompts (IGAS1, PT1)
arms.description: ChatGPT-4o image generation, new chat window per task; abstract prompts.

participants.exclusions: None reported. Sixty were recruited, 10 per EXP x ATP cell; the ANOVA error df of 54 (Tables 4 to 6) and Fig. 3 ('all 60 participants') are consistent with all 60 analyzed. Per-arm n is not printed; the 60 per arm reflects the within-person design.
participants.who: Participants grouped by design experience (non-design majors with under 1 year of training; 1 to 3 years of design training; over 3 years of professional design education or practice and led 2+ projects) and AIGC tool proficiency (low vs high). The acknowledgements thank 'experimental participants from our affiliated universities'; student status is not stated explicitly.
participants.country: not_stated (authors' affiliations and participants' universities are in China)
participants.quote: Considering operational feasibility and group balance, 60 participants were ultimately recruited, ensuring n = 10 per experimental cell to satisfy statistical power requirements.

ai_tool.name_model: Midjourney V6 (aesthetic-prioritised condition) and ChatGPT-4o image generation (instruction-following condition), both accessed March 2025
ai_tool.how_used: Participants typed prompts of the assigned type into the assigned tool and generated as many motorcycle concepts as possible in 10 minutes, then picked one representative image to submit. Settings were pre-configured by researchers; a 5-minute procedural training video gave no creative guidance.

task.description: Generate innovative motorcycle concept designs with the assigned image tool and prompt type; submit one representative image per condition (four per participant).
task.duration: 10 minutes per condition, four conditions, about 5-minute breaks between; followed by a perceived-usefulness questionnaire and a 5-minute interview

outcomes.name: Creative quality (expert rating)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two senior product-design experts, blind to condition, rated each submitted image on five 5-point items (functional completeness, formal aesthetics, technical feasibility, user orientation, overall completeness); final score = mean of the two experts. Cronbach alpha 0.847; ICC(3,2) = 0.703. Construct coded 'usefulness' because the items rate quality/feasibility rather than creativity as a whole. Repeated-measures mixed ANOVA, participant as subject (df_error 54); one image per participant per condition (four per participant, p. 7).

outcomes.name: Image-level attribute creative diversity (expert categorical coding)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Each submitted image coded by both experts on four attributes (form/structure, material and surface, conceptual style, ergonomics; Table 1); an equal-weighted average of four attribute-level variety measures V1 to V4 gives a 0-1 score per image. The formula is referred to but not printed in the PDF (p. 8). The paper states the unit is the individual image, not a set or pool, so this is attribute breadth within one output, not similarity across people's outputs; coded 'other', not 'diversity'. Analysed with an Aligned Rank Transform ANOVA because of non-normality.

eligibility.reason: All 60 participants used generative AI in every condition; the AI contrast is within person (Midjourney V6 vs ChatGPT-4o image generation, and abstract vs concrete prompts), an ai_design comparison with no no-AI arm. Condition order was counterbalanced with a 4 x 4 balanced Latin square, but the paper never says sequences were randomly allocated, so criterion 1 (randomized order for within-person designs) is unclear. Criterion 2: 60 people, all apparently analyzed (df_error 54), above 50. Criterion 3: expert-rated quality and novelty of each submitted image. Whether two commercial tools count as 'a different AI configuration' is a further judgment for review. Design experience and tool proficiency are measured, not assigned.

one_line_finding: In a within-person lab study of 60 participants, motorcycle concept images made with Midjourney V6 were rated higher than those made with ChatGPT-4o on quality (3.58 vs 3.11; diff 0.469, SE 0.107; p. 12, Table 5) and novelty (3.12 vs 2.68; diff 0.444, SE 0.141; p. 14, Table 6), with no no-AI comparison.
open_questions: Criterion 1: the 4 x 4 balanced Latin square (p. 7) counterbalances order, but random allocation of participants to sequences is not stated. Does counterbalanced order qualify as randomized order?

Does Midjourney V6 vs ChatGPT-4o (two commercial tools) count as two 'AI configurations' for an ai_design contrast? Which arm is treatment? I set Midjourney V6 as treatment and ChatGPT-4o (the general chatbot) as control; abstract prompts as treatment, concrete as control. Neither is the paper's proposed configuration.
The 'creative diversity' score is attribute breadth within one image (p. 8), not similarity across people, so it does not answer across_people. The formula is missing from the PDF.
Table 7 (p. 15) has internal inconsistencies: EXP x IGAS F = 1.018 with p = 0.903, and EXP x ATP x PT F = 0.049 with p = 0.616; ART df of 162 for within effects is not explained.
Text vs Table 3 mismatches: creative quality PT0 mean 3.46 (text p. 11) vs 3.47 (Table 3); perceived usefulness SDs 0.66/0.83 (text) vs 0.68/0.86 (Table 3) for IGAS and 0.64/0.83 vs 0.68/0.82 for PT.
Population coded 'students' from the acknowledgement thanking 'participants from our affiliated universities' (p. 17); the paper does not state student status.
notes: Arm-level means are Table 3 marginal means pooled over the other within factor; cell means appear only in Fig. 5 for quality (ChatGPT-4o concrete 3.34, abstract 2.88; Midjourney concrete/abstract labels 3.59 and 3.57 overlap, p. 13). Data availability statement: 'No datasets were generated or analysed during the current study' (p. 17). Ethics approval is mentioned without naming the body (p. 5). Statistical analysis in SPSS 27.0 with Holm-Bonferroni post hoc tests (p. 9).
